jobs.description: The University of Zurich invites applications for a professorship in philosophy of mind and language starting on 1 August 2028.The successful candidate will have an outstanding and internationally recognised research profile clearly grounded in philosophy, with demonstrated expertise in both philosophy of mind and philosophy of language, together with an extensive teaching experience. The successful candidate must also have substantial interdisciplinary expertise in at least one empirical research field relevant to the NCCR «Evolving Language», such as evolutionary language research, biological anthropology, cognitive ethology or animal communication, developmental psychology, cognitive psychology, cognitive neuroscience, computational linguistics, or generative AI. The appointee will be expected to contribute to teaching across the full range of theoretical philosophy, and it would be advantageous if they were also able to offer courses in selected areas of the history of philosophy. In addition to providing innovative contributions to research in the field, the successful candidate will be expected to collaborate in both research and teaching with colleagues within the Department of Philosophy (in particular those working on normativity), across the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, with other faculties at the University of Zurich, and with national and international partners (notably the NCCR «Evolving Language»).  Applicants must hold a PhD in Philosophy at the time of application and have an excellent record of further scholarly publications demonstrating an additional area of expertise. Depending on qualifications and experience, the position will be appointed at the level of Full Professor or Associate Professor. German is the administrative language of the University of Zurich; therefore, the successful candidate will be expected to acquire an adequate command of German within three years of appointment. The Department of Philosophy, the University of Zurich, and the wider Zurich academic environment offer a stimulating setting for research and teaching, with extensive opportunities for academic exchange and collaboration. The University of Zurich is an equal opportunities employer and committed to diversity in research and teaching. Therefore, applications from candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged. Further details and access to the application portal are available atwww.phil.uzh.ch/jobs.html.

jobs.description: The Edmond & Lily Safra Center for Ethics at Harvard University invites applications from a broad range of researchers and practitioners who will work over the course of the year on pressing issues in ethics. Faculty in arts and sciences and professional schools, postdoctoral scholars, practitioners, and researchers from industry, government, and NGOs are eligible to apply. The call for applications for the 2027-28academic year is completely open: we will consider any topicpertaining to the serious ethical questions of our time. Our Center will also becontinuing the work of ourinterdisciplinary research network exploring theethical and political dimensions of disagreement, in both its productive and unproductive varieties. Philosophers, humanists, social psychologists, and any researchers from relevant domains are invited to indicate whether their project falls into this research orbit.All eligible applicants are encouraged to apply and will be given careful consideration.As always, our goal will be to craft a cohort in which all Fellows will find valuable intellectual partnerships to support and spur their work.The ideal candidates arethose who are willing to invest time and energy into building community with the other Fellows in their cohort.Fellows-in-Residence will be expected to devote the majority of their time to their individual projects and to participate in regular work-in-progress seminars. In addition, Fellows are strongly encouraged to participate in—and contribute to—the Center's programming, which includes public lectures, themed seminars and reading groups, conferences, workshops, and lunch discussions.Fellows may be invited to teach a Harvard class during the course of their appointment.This Fellowship is residential. With the exception of travel to conferences and meetings, Fellows are expected to be in residence in the Boston areaat least four working days per week during the term, and working from the Center’s office space at least three days per week.For the last few years, the Center has offered the possibility of joint fellowship opportunities with several other Centers at Harvard. We continue to offer that possibility, with specific potential affiliations to be worked out on a case-by-case basis:Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Societyat Harvard UniversityCarr-Ryan Center for Human Rights at the Harvard Kennedy SchoolCenter for Bioethics at the Harvard Medical SchoolHutchins Center for African & African American Research at Harvard UniversityPetrie-Flom Center for Health Law Policy, Biotechnology and Bioethics at the Harvard Law SchoolApplicants will be invited to indicate on the application form whether they wish to be considered for a joint fellowship position with one of these Centers. jobs.description: Since its founding in 1986, Harvard University’sEdmond & Lily Safra Center for Ethicshas convened scholars and practitioners to confront pressing ethical questions of the time. Building on this tradition, the Center invites applications for the Ethics and Civics Postdoctoral Fellowship. This fellowship is housed in the Research & Design Studio, the Center’s innovation hub, and is designed to help a new generation of thinkers and practitioners translate ethical reflection and scholarship into practical contributions for academia and public life.The Research & Design Studio:The Research & Design Studio (R&DS) is an interdisciplinary network that bridges researchand pedagogy. Its current theme and focus are the ethical and political dimensions of disagreement: when it proves productive, how to rebuild a culture of principled disagreement, and how to navigate difference. Through this work, the R&DS seeks to strengthen civil discourse in higher education and public life, bringing together faculty, students, researchers, and practitioners to explore how we can engage across differences more constructively.Community & Collaboration:The Ethics and Civics Postdoctoral Fellowship seeksto prepare the next generation of scholars to integrate practical ethics and civil disagreement into both their research and teaching as they begin their academic careers. In addition to their individual research projects, fellows will develop pedagogical tools or practices during their time at the Center that can support their future teaching as well as contribute to the overall work of the R&DS and its Community of Practice.Fellows will work together with R&DS staff to ensure they are able to effectively translate their scholarship into practical outcomes. The fellowship seminar will include opportunities to workshop both fellows’ research and pedagogy projects over the course of the year.The fellowship is renewable for a second year at the discretion of the Center.We plan to welcome three new and up to three returning fellows each year.Fellowship Expectations:We aim to build cohorts where fellows find valuable intellectual partnerships to support and spur their work. The ideal candidates are those interested in investing time and energy into contributing to the R&DS’s research agenda and pedagogical resource development initiatives and building community with the other fellows in their cohort, while also furthering their own projects.Fellows will receive support from the Center’s research and pedagogy teams to develop their projects for a variety of audiences and to translate their research interests into practical tools and applications.Fellows may be invited to teach a Harvard class during the course of their appointment.Ethics & Civics Postdoctoral Fellows will:Work with the pedagogy team to develop tools or instructional applications related to their research and/or teaching interests.Participate in regular seminars with their cohort and others at the Center.Engage actively with the Center’s broader programming, which includes public lectures, themed seminars and reading groups, conferences, workshops, and lunch discussions.Advance their individual research projects, with the support of the Center’s research team as needed/available.Residency Requirement:This is a residential fellowship. Fellows are expected to live in the Boston area and be present at the Center at least three days per week, with at least four working days per week in the area overall. Occasional travel for conferences and other professional commitments is permitted, but Fellows should discuss their plans with the R&DS’s Director of Research and Strategic Initiativesbefore making a commitment.Eligibility:Applicants must have completed a doctoral degree no more than three years before the start of the Fellowship year.Applicants from any discipline or professional field will be considered. Those who have previously held a yearlong residential Fellowship at the Center are not eligible; this limitation does not apply to former Undergraduate Fellows or former Graduate Fellows. The Research & Design Studio works over the course of the academic year, and is open to all applicants who meet the above criteria, regardless of citizenship.Please note that advanced language skills in both written and spoken English are required for Fellows at the Center. Fellows are expected to discuss and/or present their work in English and are encouraged to participate in informal discussions with faculty and students with related interests. Application materials, including writing samples, should be in English. If offered a fellowship, non-native English speakers who cannot demonstrate their proficiency through (1) completion of a degree from an English-speaking institution of higher education or (2) satisfactory TOEFL or IELTS scores will be contacted by the Center staff to arrange for further evaluation as needed.Stipend:The stipend for post-doctoral fellows will be $7,000/month for the 2027-28academic year, which runs from the start of September to the end of June. We also provide a research allowance of up to $3,000 per academic year for approved expenses directly related to your work, such as travel, books, and research assistance.

jobs.description: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) is seeking a distinguished scholar to become the next Inamori Professor in Ethics and Director of the Inamori International Center for Ethics and Excellence (Inamori Center). A$125 million giftfrom the Mandel Foundation in 2026 includes support for a new humanities building and funding for integrating humanities with STEM approaches, while the University’s new $300 millionInterdisciplinary Science and Engineering Buildingbrings together researchers across Arts and Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. This environment creates fertile ground for the Director to forge connections across artificial intelligence, technology, engineering, medicine, neuroscience, the humanities, and other fields, engaging scholars, students, and external partners around some of the most consequential ethical questions facing society.The Director will also provide leadership for the Inamori Ethics Prize, the Center’s prestigious international award recognizing individuals whose ethical leadership has significantly improved the condition of humankind. articulate a compelling vision for the Center’s next chapter and translate that vision into programs, partnerships, and initiatives with meaningful impact.Advance the Center as an interdisciplinary hub for ethical inquiry, connecting scholars and practitioners across fields and schools, and providing ethics support for complex research projects that include a significant ethical dimension.Develop programming that engages consequential ethical questions emerging from areas such as artificial intelligence, technology, engineering, medicine, neuroscience, the humanities, and other disciplines.Provide leadership for the Inamori Ethics Prize and identify opportunities to increase its visibility, reach, and impact.Provide effective administrative and operational leadership for the Center, including stewardship of its approximately $400,000 annual budget.Serve as a visible ambassador for the Center and strengthen its national and international profile.MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSThe successful candidate will bring:A record of scholarship and academic achievement appropriate for appointment at the rank of full professor with tenure at Case Western Reserve University.International recognition as a scholar and thought leader in their field.An outstanding record of excellence in research, teaching, and mentorship.A scholarly focus in ethics or demonstrated integration of ethical inquiry into their scholarship and teaching.A strong record of interdisciplinary engagement and collaboration.Demonstrated leadership experience within an academic or research environment.The ability to develop and advance a compelling strategic vision for the Inamori Center.About Case Western Reserve UniversityAs the fastest-growing research university in the new_jobs.description: James Mitchell Endowed Chair and Arts & Humanities Artificial Intelligence Institute Center DirectorRank: Advanced Associate Professor or Professor College of Arts and SciencesPosition Overview The Ohio State University seeks the James Mitchell Endowed Chair who will be a center director to provide ambitious and innovative leadership for its newly established Arts and Humanities Artificial Intelligence Institute (AHAII). The aim is to make Ohio State a national hub in the conversation about what it means to be human in the age of AI. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. The director will serve as the administrative head of an emerging and thriving institute, with oversight of facilities, budget, and strategic direction. In addition to their role as the institute leader and administrator, the director will also be a dedicated teacher and distinguished scholar, with a record of accomplishment to merit a tenure-track appointment in an Arts or Humanities department as an advanced Associate Professor or Professor. The new director is expected to foster a collegial and interdisciplinary culture among a community of faculty, staff, and students from varied disciplinary backgrounds. They will be an advocate for the institute and its affiliated faculty and students, providing support and mentorship for scholarly activity while amplifying the voice of the arts and humanities in conversations around AI. Applying their knowledge in developing approaches, manifestations, and discourse tied to matters of AI, the director will guide institute affiliates, outreach endeavors, and student education. The director will have the opportunity to shape renovation plans for AHAII in Hughes Hall, a historic building on the oval and future home of our English Department. The director should be poised to engage with students, faculty, staff, and alumni to build collaborations with arts and humanities departments and interdisciplinary initiatives across the College of Arts and Sciences and the broader university community, Ohio State’s five regional campuses, and community organizations in Ohio and beyond.   The successful candidate will be a dedicated educator and a recognized scholar and/or practitioner with expertise in one or more scholarly areas involving artificial intelligence and arts or humanities and will have a 50% FTE (Full Time Equivalent) faculty appointment in an appointment in one of the 21 Arts and Humanities departments in the College of Arts and Sciences with the other 50% FTE appointment as AHAII director.   Performance ObjectivesTo new_jobs.description: Endowed Professorships for Democracy and Constitutional GovernanceUniversity of VirginiaCharlottesville, VAThe College and Graduate School of Arts & Sciences at the University of Virginia (UVA) invites applications and nominations to fill three endowed professorships devoted to the study of democracy and constitutional governance:The Jefferson Scholars Foundation Distinguished Professorship in Political Economy, Law & Democracy –appointed as a tenured full professorThe John S. Lillard Jefferson Scholars Foundation Professorship in American Constitutionalism and Democracy –appointed as a tenured associate or full professorThe Cory Chair in Political Philosophy, Policy, and Law –appointed as a tenured associate or full professorAs a public institution founded by Thomas Jefferson, the University of Virginia has long embraced itsmissionof forming free and thoughtful citizen leaders through a liberal arts education. To fill these professorships, UVA seeks innovative and collaborative academic leaders who are eager to build on the University’s premier position among American universities in research and teaching on the historical, legal, and institutional foundations of liberal democratic societies. The endowed professors will join a distinguished faculty spanning disciplines across the University, including colleagues in theSchool of Lawand theKarsh Institute of Democracy. Each professorship will be affiliated with one of two longstanding programs in the College: theProgram on Constitutionalism and Democracy(PCD) or the Program onPolitical Philosophy, Policy, and Law(PPL).Ideal candidates for these positions will embody a combination of scholarly distinction, pedagogical excellence, and institutional citizenship. They will bring a distinguished record in scholarship, teaching, and service appropriate to rank. The Cory Chair and Lillard Professor may be appointed at the rank of Associate Professor or full Professor while the Jefferson Scholars Foundation Distinguished Professorship in Political Economy, Law & Democracy will be a senior scholar at the rank of Professor. Candidates for all three chairs will demonstrate distinction in their field and in scholarship related to such themes as liberal democracy and constitutionalism, political economy, legal thought and the historical development of law and legal institutions, American civic thought and practice, and/or the intellectual foundations of public life; a commitment to undergraduate education; an ability to collaborate across academic boundaries and contribute to the development of innovative programs; a commitment to intellectual pluralism and open inquiry; and alignment with UVA’s mission, embracing the University’s values of service, discovery, and the formation of citizen-leaders through a liberal arts education. While the endowed professorships will be housed in a College of Arts and Sciences department appropriate to the chairholder’s field of specialization, this is a multi-disciplinary search, allowing for departmental collaboration. Outstanding scholars in any field whose scholarly profiles fit the position description are encouraged to apply.A multi-disciplinary search committee has been formed, chaired by ProfessorWilliam Hitchcock,and will be supported by Isaacson, Miller, the national executive search firm. Screening of applications will begin immediately and continue until the search is complete. Inquiries, nominations, and applications should be submitted in confidence through the Isaacson, Miller website:https://www.imsearch.com/open-searches/university-virginia/endowed-professorships-democracy-and-constitutional-governanceThe University of Virginia is an equal opportunity employer. All interested persons are encouraged to apply, including veterans and individuals with disabilities.
